This Stealthy Box Trailer Hides a Luxury Tiny Home With Two Beds and Beautiful Styling
15 photos
Photo: Tilghman Trailers
While some people cringe at the idea of tiny living, others consider having a smaller living space a worthwhile trade-off, especially if that living space is mobile, as it would allow them to travel more, explore the outdoors, live more simply, and spend more time in nature. That is exactly what the XL adventure is designed to offer.
Larger and more commodious than a camper van, yet easier to tow and maneuver than a full-size RV, this box trailer conversion offers a comfortable little home on wheels with everything needed for off-grid living.
Built by Tilghman Trailers, the XL Adventure doesn’t pretend to replace a conventional house, nor does it try to squeeze all the features of a large motorhome into a tiny trailer. Instead, it combines a discreet exterior with an interior that has been transformed into a beautiful and comfortable living space that offers two beds, a full kitchen, an indoor shower, and the essential modern off-grid systems.
Tilghman Trailers was founded by Keon Tilghman, a man who built his first camper van in 2019 and headed to California to experience van life firsthand. He became passionate about turning small spaces into places that feel like home, and his passion only grew with mastery. Through YouTube tutorials and plenty of hands-on learning, he honed his building skills and founded Tilghman Trailers.
Photo: Tilghman Trailers Today, his company specializes in turning stealth cargo trailers into semi-custom tiny homes designed for adventure, with practical layouts, modern finishes, and handcrafted furniture. Customers can choose between two Tilghman Trailers models: the Classic and the XL.
As suggested by its name, the XL Adventure is the largest model of the two and is designed for traveling couples or small families. It boasts a dual-axle design and measures 18.9 feet (5.7 meters) in overall length, including the hitch, and 8 feet (2.4 meters) in width. It’s 9.4 feet (2.8 meters) high, and its estimated finished weight is approximately 5,000 pounds (2,267 kg), which means it can be safely towed by mid-size or larger SUVs and light-duty half-ton trucks.
One of the first things that some people might find appealing about this rig is its inconspicuous exterior. Finished in simple gray paint, the trailer might be a great option for those looking for a stealth build. Apart from a couple of windows, the entry door, and an awning on the campsite, there is little to suggest that this is more than a regular cargo trailer.
At the rear, owners can choose between traditional barn doors and a ramp, and the exterior color can also be changed to charcoal gray or white.
Photo: Tilghman Trailers The interior of the XL Adventure is only 14 feet (4.2 meters) long and 7 feet (2.1 meters) wide, but Keon got creative with the use of space. By using clever solutions like an elevator bed and hidden storage, he created a livable habitat with sleeping for four and all the essentials for life on the road.
There is no separation wall inside this trailer apart from the bathroom walls, and the living space feels like an open, studio apartment on wheels with a clean, nature-inspired palette of sage green, light gray, and warm wood tones. Baltic birch is used on the walls, LifeProof vinyl on the floors, and all the furniture is handcrafted.
Dimmable indirect lighting lets you create a nice ambiance in the evening, while the large doorway at the rear creates an open, luminous, and airy atmosphere during the day.
Photo: Tilghman Trailers The space is dominated by a comfortable modular sofa that faces an open-concept media wall with a large flat-screen TV framed by minimalistic wood shelving for books and decorations. It’s a multifunctional space for relaxation and other daily activities.
A compact kitchen occupies the front area of the trailer. It has both low and upper cabinets, which are paired with a 53-inch butcher block countertop integrating a stainless steel sink and an Empava induction cooktop. A large fridge-freezer is also included in its dedicated cabinet near the bathroom.
Speaking of the bathroom, considering the size of the trailer, don’t expect a full bath. It is a small wet bath finished with waterproof vinyl tile, which includes a shower, a small ledge for toiletries, and a dry-flush toilet.
But one of the most interesting elements of the design is the double-bed arrangement. The sofa pulls into a comfortable bed for two, and the builder added an elevator bed just above it, which is electrically operated and stays out of the way when it’s not needed. The upper bed is a standard queen size, while the lower one is even larger.
Photo: Tilghman Trailers For extended boondocking and off-grid trips, the XL Adventure trailer comes equipped with 600 watts of solar panels on a roof, a 600Ah lithium battery bank, and a 3,000W Victron MultiPlus inverter/charger that manages the electrical supply. A shore-power hookup is available. For your water needs, the trailer carries a 33-gallon fresh-water tank and a 30-gallon gray-water tank.
Other standard equipment includes a 7-gallon Basch water heater, 12V air conditioning, a diesel heater, leveling jacks, and a storage box mounted at the hitch.
Though the Tilghman XL Adventure can only be ordered with a fixed layout and the furniture design remains unchanged, owners can personalize the interior with their choice of finishes, including interior wall paint, flooring, furniture door-face finishes, and bathroom wall finishes.
Designed to appeal to travelers, nomads, and seasonal campers, the Tilghman XL Adventure box trailer offers a discreet and well-equipped mobile living space. Pricing starts at $70,000.
